pages.title: Example: one Cloudflare token, several zones
pages.summary: Share one Cloudflare configuration between two targets, each supplying its own zone, so the wildcard certificate of each domain renews into the right zone.
pages.markdown:
**Goal.** Your company has two domains on Cloudflare, `example.com` and
`example.net`. lcm issues a wildcard certificate for each. Whenever either
certificate is issued or renewed, it should be uploaded to its own zone,
without anyone clicking **Deploy**. You have one Cloudflare API token that
may edit SSL certificates in both zones.

**Plan.** One Cloudflare configuration holds the token and leaves the
**Zone ID** to its targets. Two targets, one per domain, each match their
wildcard certificate and supply their zone.

## 1. The shared configuration

In **Deployer → Configurations**, create:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `cloudflare-main` |
| Provider | Cloudflare |
| Zone ID | *(empty)* |
| API token | the token (permission Zone → SSL and Certificates → Edit) |

Choose **Check settings**. Because the zone is missing, the answer is
"Checked. Not tested here: Zone ID — each target supplies it." Save. In the
list, **Deploy** is disabled for this configuration: it can only be deployed
through a target.

## 2. Two targets

Create two targets in **Deployer → Targets**, each with
**Auto-deploy on issue/renewal** on and `cloudflare-main` attached:

| Target | Common name (regex) | Zone ID under **Settings per configuration** |
|---|---|---|
| `example-com` | `*.example.com` | zone ID of example.com |
| `example-net` | `*.example.net` | zone ID of example.net |

`*.example.com` matches the wildcard certificate itself (its common name is
`*.example.com`) and any single-label name such as `www.example.com`, but not
the `example.net` certificate. Each certificate therefore reaches exactly one
target.

The same through the API. Create the target with
`POST /api/deployer/v1/targets`:

```json
{
  "name": "example-com",
  "auto_deploy": true,
  "certificate_filters": [{"common_name_pattern": "*.example.com"}]
}
```

Then attach the configuration and supply the zone (a 32-character hex
string) with `POST /api/deployer/v1/targets/<target id>/configurations`:

```json
{
  "configuration_ids": ["<cloudflare-main id>"],
  "config_overrides": {
    "<cloudflare-main id>": {"zone_id": "023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353"}
  }
}
```

## 3. What happens on renewal

When lcm renews `*.example.com`, the deployer creates a parent job for
`example-com` with one child job for `cloudflare-main`, triggered
`auto_renewal`. The child deploys with the token from `cloudflare-main` and
the zone from `example-com`. The `example-net` target does not match and
creates no job.

On **Deployer → Jobs** you see:

| Type | Trigger | Status |
|---|---|---|
| parent | `auto_renewal` | `completed` |
| child | `auto_renewal` | `completed` |

## Variations

- **Add another endpoint.** Attach a second configuration (for example a
  FortiGate) to `example-com`. The next renewal creates two children; if one
  fails, the parent becomes `partial`. See [jobs](../guides/jobs.md).
- **Rotate the token.** Edit `cloudflare-main` and type the new token. Both
  targets use it from the next deployment on.
- **Forgot the zone?** A target that attaches `cloudflare-main` without a
  zone shows "Missing required values: Zone ID", and its jobs fail with
  `configuration incomplete: Zone ID must be provided by the target`.

Related: [auto-deploy](../guides/auto-deploy.md),
[configurations](../guides/configurations.md).

pages.title: Get started
pages.summary: Create a test configuration with the Dummy provider and deploy a certificate to it.
pages.markdown:
This walk-through deploys a certificate to the **Dummy** provider, which
installs nothing and always succeeds. It shows the whole flow without touching
real infrastructure.

You need the `configurations:manage` and `deploy:execute` permissions (the
*Deployer administrator* role has both), and `jobs:read` to watch the job.

## 1. Create a configuration

1. Open **Deployer → Configurations** and choose **New configuration**.
2. Give it a name, for example `test-dummy`.
3. In **Provider**, choose **Dummy (testing)**.
4. Leave **Fail** off and choose **Check settings**. The drawer answers
   "The settings are valid."
5. Choose **Save**. The configuration appears in the list with status
   `active`.

## 2. Find a certificate

The deployer deploys certificates that lcm issued. Open **Certificates**,
pick a certificate (or issue one) and copy its ID.

## 3. Deploy

1. Back in **Deployer → Configurations**, choose **Deploy** on the
   `test-dummy` row.
2. Paste the certificate ID into **Certificate ID** and confirm.
3. A message confirms that the deployment started and shows the job ID.

## 4. Watch the job

Open **Deployer → Jobs**. The new job is a *direct* job triggered `manual`.
It moves from `pending` through `processing` to `completed` without a page
refresh. Open it to see its **History**: one `deploy` entry with result
`success` and its duration.

## Next steps

- Set up a real provider: [manage configurations](guides/configurations.md).
- Let renewals deploy themselves: [auto-deploy](guides/auto-deploy.md).
- If the job fails, see [jobs](guides/jobs.md).

pages.title: Deploy automatically on issue and renewal
pages.summary: Use a target with certificate filters and auto-deploy so new and renewed certificates install themselves.
pages.markdown:
A **target** groups configurations. With **auto-deploy** on, the deployer
watches lcm: whenever lcm issues or renews a certificate that matches one of
the target's filters, it deploys that certificate to every configuration
attached to the target. No one has to click **Deploy** when a certificate
renews.

Creating and changing targets needs `targets:manage`.

## Create a target

1. Open **Deployer → Targets** and choose **New target**.
2. Enter a **Name** and, optionally, a **Description**.
3. Turn on **Auto-deploy on issue/renewal**.
4. Under **Certificate filters**, choose **Add filter** and fill in the
   fields you want to match (see below).
5. Under **Attached configurations**, tick the configurations to deploy to.
6. If a configuration needs values from this target, open it under
   **Settings per configuration** and fill them in.
7. Choose **Save**.

## How filters match

Each filter has these fields. Empty fields are ignored.

| Field | Matches | How |
|---|---|---|
| Issuer (exact) | the certificate's issuer name | exact text |
| Common name (regex) | the subject common name | pattern |
| SAN (regex) | any one of the subject alternative names | pattern |
| Organization (exact) | the subject O | exact text |

Through the API a filter can also match `subject_org_unit` and
`subject_country`, both exact.

- All filled fields of one filter must match (AND).
- A target with several filters deploys when **any** filter matches (OR).
- A target with **no** filters, or with an empty filter, matches every
  certificate. Be careful with auto-deploy on such a target.

A pattern is either:

- a leading-wildcard name such as `*.example.com`, which matches exactly one
  label in front of the domain: `www.example.com` and `*.example.com` match,
  `a.b.example.com` and `example.com` do not; or
- a regular expression (RE2 syntax), always matched against the whole value:
  `api\.example\.(com|net)` matches `api.example.com` but not
  `api.example.com.evil.net`.

A pattern that is not a valid expression is matched as plain text. A
pattern longer than 256 characters never matches.

## What happens on an event

When lcm publishes `certificate.issued` or `certificate.renewed`, the
deployer fetches the certificate and checks every target with auto-deploy on.
For each matching target that has at least one attached configuration it
creates a **parent** job with one **child** job per configuration. The jobs
are triggered `event` for a new certificate and `auto_renewal` for a renewal.
Follow them on the [Jobs](jobs.md) page.

Certificates issued while the deployer is not running are not replayed when
it starts again: deploy those by hand.

## Supply or change settings per target

Under **Settings per configuration**, each attached configuration shows the
fields its provider lets a target change. Leave a field empty to inherit the
configuration's value. A **Must supply** badge marks fields the configuration
left for its targets; deployments to the target fail until they are filled.

Overrides never carry credentials, and fields that decide where credentials
go (URLs, the appliance host) are never overridable. See
[target overrides](../reference.md#target-overrides).

## Deploy to a target by hand

The portal deploys by hand to one configuration at a time. To deploy a
certificate to every configuration of a target at once, call the API with the
`deploy:execute` permission: `POST /api/deployer/v1/deploy/target` with
the `X-CSRF-Token` header and this JSON body:

```json
{"certificate_id": "<lcm certificate id>", "target_id": "<target id>"}
```

The answer is `202` with the parent `job_id`. A target with no attached
configurations is refused with `422 validation_failed`.

pages.title: Manage configurations
pages.summary: Add a provider configuration, test its connection, keep credentials safe and leave settings for targets to supply.
pages.markdown:
A configuration is one endpoint the deployer can install certificates on: a
provider, its settings and its credentials. Everyone with
`configurations:read` can list and open configurations; creating, changing,
testing and deleting them needs `configurations:manage`.

## Create a configuration

1. Open **Deployer → Configurations** and choose **New configuration**.
2. Enter a **Name** (up to 100 characters) and, optionally, a
   **Description**.
3. Choose the **Provider**. The drawer shows that provider's fields in three
   groups: **Connection**, **Credentials** and **Options**. Required fields
   are marked, and defaults are filled in.
4. Run the provider's check (see below), then choose **Save**.

The provider cannot be changed after saving. To move an endpoint to another
provider, create a new configuration.

## Test before you save

Each provider has one check button in the drawer:

| Button | Providers | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Test connection** | F5 BIG-IP, FortiGate, Webhook | contacts the endpoint with the entered credentials |
| **Check settings** | AWS Certificate Manager, Cloudflare, Dummy | checks the values without deploying anything |
| **Preview hosts** | Inventory agent | lists the hosts the selection matches and whether their agents can receive certificates |

"Connection successful." means the endpoint accepted the credentials. If the
endpoint refuses them, the check fails with `credentials_rejected` and
nothing is saved.

## Credentials are write-only

- Secret fields (passwords, API tokens, secret keys) are never shown again
  after saving. The list shows **Credentials stored** instead.
- When you edit a configuration, leave a secret blank to keep the stored
  value; type a new value to replace it.
- If you change where credentials go (a URL or the appliance host), you must
  re-enter every stored secret in the same save. This stops a changed
  destination from receiving the old secrets.
- Webhook custom headers may not carry authentication (`Authorization`,
  `Cookie`, or names containing token, secret, key, auth, password and
  similar). Use the credential fields instead.

## Leave a setting for the targets

Some settings may be changed per target (for example the Cloudflare
`zone_id` or the BIG-IP `ssl_profile`). A *required* setting of this kind may
be left empty on a shared configuration: every target that uses the
configuration then supplies it. Such a configuration:

- cannot be deployed on its own: its **Deploy** button is disabled, with a
  hint naming the fields the target must supply;
- is deployed through a target, by [auto-deploy](auto-deploy.md) or by
  deploying to the target.

Settings that decide where credentials go (URLs, the appliance host) and the
TLS and header settings can never be changed by a target. The
[reference](../reference.md#target-overrides) lists what each provider
allows.

## Errors on save

A save that fails validation highlights the field and names it, for example
`config.region` or `credentials.api_token`. The value you typed is never
repeated in the error. Changing a configuration so that a target using it
would lose a required value is refused, and the error lists those targets.

## Delete a configuration

Open the configuration, choose **Delete** and confirm. The configuration is
also detached from every target that used it. Jobs that already ran stay in
the job list.

pages.title: Follow, retry, verify and roll back jobs
pages.summary: Read job status and history, understand automatic retries, and retry, cancel, verify or roll back a deployment.
pages.markdown:
Every deployment is a job. Open **Deployer → Jobs** to see them, newest
first. The list updates live: you do not need to refresh. You can filter it
by status and job type.

## Job types

- **direct** — one certificate to one configuration (the **Deploy** button).
- **parent** — one certificate to a target. It does not deploy anything
  itself; it shows the combined outcome of its children.
- **child** — the part of a parent job for one attached configuration.

A parent is `completed` when all children completed, `failed` when all
failed, and `partial` when some failed. Its progress is the share of
children that finished.

## Read a job

Open a job to see:

- **Certificate** and **Serial** of the deployed certificate;
- **Retries**, as used / allowed, for example `1 / 3`;
- **Message**, the latest progress note;
- the error of the last failure (titled **Deployment failed** while the job
  is failed). It is the provider's or lcm's own message, with credentials
  removed, so it usually names the real cause;
- **History**: every deploy, verify and rollback attempt with its result and
  duration;
- **Child deployments** for a parent job;
- **Hosts** for the Inventory agent provider: the state each host reported.

## Automatic retries

When a deployment fails, the job goes to `retrying` and runs again after a
delay that grows each time (by default 1, 2, then 4 minutes). After the last
retry the job is `failed`. Some failures are not retried because retrying
cannot help, for example:

- `configuration incomplete: … must be provided by the target` — a required
  value is missing; fill it in on the configuration or the target;
- `certificate has no stored private key` — lcm holds no key for this
  certificate, and the provider needs one;
- `credentials unavailable` — the stored credentials could not be opened;
- `no hosts matched` — the Inventory agent selection matches no host;
- a FortiGate `MANUAL REVIEW REQUIRED` stop.

## Actions

The buttons in the job drawer need `jobs:manage` (Cancel, Retry) or
`deploy:execute` (Verify, Rollback).

| Action | Shown for | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Cancel** | `pending`, `processing`, `retrying` | marks the job `cancelled`; for a parent, also its unfinished children |
| **Retry** | `failed`, `partial` | queues the job again, if it has retries left |
| **Verify** | direct and child jobs | asks the endpoint whether the certificate is installed; adds a `verify` history entry |
| **Rollback** | direct and child jobs | asks the provider to undo the deployment; adds a `rollback` history entry |

Notes:

- A parent job only sums up its children. To run a partial deployment again,
  open each failed child and retry it.
- Retry does nothing once all retries are used up (`3 / 3`). Through the API,
  `POST /api/deployer/v1/jobs/<id>/retry?force=true` resets the count and
  queues the job again.
- Verify and Rollback on a provider without that capability answer
  `409 unsupported`. AWS Certificate Manager, Cloudflare and Inventory agent
  have no rollback. See [providers](../index.md#providers).

## Simulate a failure

To see retries and errors without touching real infrastructure, edit a
**Dummy** configuration, turn on **Fail** and deploy to it.

## Who sees job events

Live job updates go only to users who hold `jobs:read`. Users without it do
not see the Jobs page and receive no job events.

pages.title: Deployer
pages.summary: Install lcm-issued certificates on cloud services, load balancers, firewalls, webhooks and Linux hosts, by hand or automatically on issue and renewal.
pages.markdown:
The deployer takes certificates issued by **lcm** (the Certificates module) and
installs them on your infrastructure. It can deploy on demand, or
automatically whenever lcm issues or renews a certificate that matches your
rules.

## Concepts

- **Configuration** — one endpoint the deployer can install a certificate on:
  a provider (for example Cloudflare or FortiGate), its settings and its
  credentials. Credentials are encrypted and never shown again after you save
  them.
- **Target** — a named group of configurations, with optional
  **certificate filters** and an **auto-deploy** switch. A target can also
  change some provider settings for each configuration it uses.
- **Job** — one deployment of one certificate. Deploying to a configuration
  creates a *direct* job; deploying to a target creates a *parent* job with one
  *child* job per configuration. Jobs retry on failure and update live in the
  portal.

The deployer never stores certificate bytes. At deploy time it fetches the
certificate, chain and (when the provider needs it) the private key from lcm,
hands them to the provider and drops them.

## Providers

| Provider | Installs on | Verify | Rollback |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|
| AWS Certificate Manager (`aws_acm`) | ACM in one region | yes | no |
| Cloudflare (`cloudflare`) | a Cloudflare zone | yes | no |
| F5 BIG-IP (`bigip`) | a BIG-IP partition, optionally a client-SSL profile | yes | yes |
| FortiGate (`fortigate`) | a FortiGate VDOM and its SSL profiles | yes | yes |
| Webhook (`webhook`) | any HTTP endpoint that accepts a JSON POST | yes | yes |
| Inventory agent (`inventory-agent`) | Linux hosts running the go-tangra-inventory agent | yes | no |
| Dummy (`dummy`) | nothing: for testing | yes | yes |

## Pages in the portal

| Page | Shows | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | jobs by status, recent success rate, recent errors | `stats:read` |
| Targets | deployment targets, filters, attached configurations | `targets:read` |
| Configurations | provider configurations; **Deploy** | `configurations:read` |
| Jobs | deployment jobs, their history and actions | `jobs:read` |

Your role decides what you can do; see [permissions and roles](reference.md#permissions-and-roles).

## Where to go next

- [Get started](getting-started.md): your first deployment in five minutes.
- [Manage configurations](guides/configurations.md)
- [Deploy automatically on issue and renewal](guides/auto-deploy.md)
- [Follow, retry, verify and roll back jobs](guides/jobs.md)
- [Example: one wildcard certificate, several zones](examples/wildcard-several-zones.md)
- [Reference](reference.md): fields, states, triggers and limits.

pages.title: Operate the deployer
pages.summary: Configuration keys and defaults, the service policies the deployer needs from lcm, auth and inventory, and fixes for common start-up and deployment errors.
pages.markdown:
The deployer runs as `deployersvc` (image `ghcr.io/go-tangra/go-tangra-deployer`).

```sh
deployersvc -config /app/config.yaml             # serve; applies migrations
deployersvc bootstrap -config /app/config.yaml   # apply migrations and exit
deployersvc version
```

At start it enrolls for its SVID `spiffe://<trust domain>/svc/deployer`,
migrates its TimescaleDB schema, serves the module API and `deployer.v1` gRPC,
registers with the gateway and registers its permissions and roles with auth.

## Configuration

The file is YAML. Unknown keys are refused, so a typo stops the service at
start with `config: <file>: ...`. Besides the framework keys (`service_name`,
`trust_domain`, `env`, `identity`, `authz`, `server`, `admin`, `discovery`,
`limits`) the deployer reads:

| Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `db.dsn` | — | required; in production `sslmode=verify-full` (or `verify-ca`) |
| `db.migrate_dsn` | — | owner connection used for migrations |
| `db.max_conns` | 16 | |
| `valkey.addresses` | — | required; the platform event bus |
| `valkey.username`, `valkey.password`, `valkey.ca_file` | — | Valkey user `deployer` over TLS |
| `valkey.allow_plaintext` | false | development only; refused in production |
| `kek.source` | `file` | `file` (with `kek.path`) or `env` (with `kek.env`): the 32-byte key that seals provider credentials |
| `jobs.workers` | 5 | 1–64 |
| `jobs.interval_seconds` | 5 | 1–60, how often workers look for due jobs |
| `jobs.lease_seconds` | 300 | interval–3600, how long a claimed job stays claimed |
| `jobs.retry_delay_seconds` | 60 | 1–3600, first retry delay |
| `jobs.backoff_multiplier` | 2.0 | 1–10, growth of the delay per retry |
| `jobs.job_timeout_seconds` | 300 | 10–3600, one deployment attempt |
| `jobs.cleanup_days` | 30 | 1–3650, job retention |
| `jobs.max_retries` | 3 | 0–20; checked at start, but jobs are currently created with 3 retries |
| `events.enabled` | true | auto-deploy consumer of `certificate.issued` / `certificate.renewed` |
| `gateway.service` | `gateway` | mesh name of the gateway; the only peer allowed to fetch the help pages |
| `gateway.issuer` | — | required, an `https://` origin: the platform token issuer |
| `lcm.service` | `lcm` | where certificates are downloaded from |
| `inventory.service` | empty | set (for example `inventory`) to enable the Inventory agent provider |
| `enroll.*` | — | `enabled`, `enroll_url`, `lcm_grpc`, `tenant_id`, `token_file`, `state_file` for SVID enrollment |
| `limits_deployer.*` | 16 MiB / 16 KiB / 256 | `backup_max_bytes`, `config_max_bytes`, `filter_max_length`; range-checked at start |

Auto-deploy reads the event stream of the tenant named in
`enroll.tenant_id`. The consumer starts at the stream's current end, so events
published while the deployer was down are not replayed.

## Service policies

The deployer's own policy must let the gateway in. The usual rule covers the
browser API, health probes and the help pages (`GET /docs/v1/bundle`):

```yaml
rules:
  - id: gateway-forwards
    from: ["spiffe://<trust domain>/svc/gateway"]
    to: ["deployer"]
    operations: ["GET *", "HEAD *", "POST *", "PUT *"]
    effect: allow
```

Other modules must admit `spiffe://<trust domain>/svc/deployer`:

| Module | Operation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| lcm | `/lcm.v1.Certificates/Download` | fetch certificate, chain and key at deploy time |
| auth | `/auth.v1.Profiles/ListMembers` | address job events to users holding `jobs:read` |
| inventory | `inventory.v1.CertificateDeliveryService` methods | Inventory agent provider; inventory's `cert_delivery.sources` must also list `deployer` |

For the Inventory agent provider the deployer also needs
`discovery.static.inventory` and `inventory: { service: inventory }`.

## Troubleshooting

**The service refuses to start with `config: ...`.** The message names the
key and its allowed range. Common ones: `db.dsn must use sslmode=verify-full`
in production, `gateway.issuer must be an https origin`, `kek.path is
required for kek.source file`.

**The service refuses to start with `help docs: ...`.** The help pages built
into the binary are invalid. This is caught by `tangra-docs lint` in CI; a
build that skips CI must be rebuilt.

**Jobs fail with `certificate fetch failed` and keep retrying.** lcm is
unreachable or its policy does not allow `/lcm.v1.Certificates/Download` for
the deployer. Check the lcm policy and `discovery.static.lcm`.

**Jobs fail with `certificate has no stored private key`.** lcm keeps no private
key for that certificate, and the provider needs one. Reissue the
certificate in lcm so that lcm retains its key. The job is not retried.

**Jobs fail with `credentials unavailable`.** The stored credentials cannot be
opened with the current key-encryption key. Make sure `kek` points at the
same key as when the configuration was saved; otherwise re-enter the
credentials.

**The Jobs page does not update live.** The log shows `deployer: job event
not sent: readers unavailable`: auth is unreachable, or its policy does not
allow `/auth.v1.Profiles/ListMembers`. Events are dropped rather than sent to
the whole tenant; the Jobs page still shows the state on reload. A new grant
of `jobs:read` takes effect within about 30 seconds.

**New certificates are not deployed automatically.** Check that
`events.enabled` is true, that the target has auto-deploy on, a matching
filter and at least one attached configuration, and that the certificate was
issued in the tenant named by `enroll.tenant_id`.

**Role changes are missing in auth.** Look for `auth registration: ...` in
the log. The deployer registers every five minutes; a revoked built-in grant
is withdrawn only by an auth that supports `declares_builtin_grants`.

pages.title: Reference
pages.summary: Job, target and configuration fields, job states and triggers, filter fields, target overrides per provider, permissions, roles, API routes and limits.
pages.markdown:
## Job fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | job ID |
| `type` | `direct`, `parent` or `child` |
| `certificate_id` | the lcm certificate deployed |
| `certificate_serial` | its serial number |
| `deployment_target_id` | the target (parent jobs) |
| `target_configuration_id` | the configuration (direct and child jobs) |
| `parent_job_id` | the parent (child jobs) |
| `status` | see [job states](#job-states) |
| `status_message` | the latest progress note or outcome |
| `error` | cause of the last failure, credentials removed; cleared by a success |
| `progress` | 0–100; for a parent, the share of finished children |
| `retry_count` / `max_retries` | automatic retries used / allowed (3) |
| `triggered_by` | see [triggers](#triggers) |
| `created_at`, `completed_at` | timestamps |

## Job states

| State | Meaning | Final |
|---|---|:-:|
| `pending` | waiting for a worker | |
| `processing` | running | |
| `retrying` | failed, another attempt is scheduled | |
| `completed` | deployed (parent: all children completed) | yes |
| `partial` | parent only: some children failed | yes |
| `failed` | failed and no retries left, or a failure retrying cannot fix | yes |
| `cancelled` | cancelled by a user, or its parent was cancelled | yes |

`failed` and `partial` jobs can be retried; see [jobs](guides/jobs.md#actions).

## Triggers

| `triggered_by` | Set when |
|---|---|
| `manual` | a user or a service deployed by hand |
| `event` | auto-deploy on `certificate.issued` |
| `auto_renewal` | auto-deploy on `certificate.renewed` |

## History entries

Each attempt adds an entry with `action` (`deploy`, `verify`, `rollback`),
`result` (`success`, `failure`, `partial`), a `message` and `duration_ms`.

## Configuration fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1–100 characters, unique in the tenant |
| `provider_type` | `aws_acm`, `bigip`, `cloudflare`, `dummy`, `fortigate`, `inventory-agent`, `webhook`; fixed after creation |
| `config` | provider settings |
| `has_credentials` | credentials are stored (their values are never returned) |
| `target_supplied` | required settings left for targets to supply |
| `status` | `active`, `inactive` or `error`; only an `active` configuration can be deployed |
| `last_deployment_at` | time of the last successful deployment |

## Target fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1–100 characters |
| `auto_deploy` | deploy on matching issue and renewal events |
| `certificate_filters` | list of filters, OR between filters, AND within one |
| `configuration_ids` | attached configurations |
| `config_overrides` | per configuration ID, the settings the target supplies or changes |
| `missing_required` | per configuration, required settings still missing |

### Certificate filter fields

| Field | Compared with | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `issuer_name` | issuer name | exact |
| `common_name_pattern` | subject CN | pattern |
| `san_pattern` | each SAN | pattern |
| `subject_organization` | subject O | exact |
| `subject_org_unit` | subject OU | exact |
| `subject_country` | subject C | exact |

Patterns: `*.domain` matches one label in front of the domain; anything
else is an RE2 expression matched against the whole value. Unknown fields
are refused (`400 malformed_body`).

## Target overrides

A target may supply or change only these settings. Credentials, URLs, the
appliance host and TLS and header settings are never overridable.

| Provider | Overridable settings |
|---|---|
| AWS Certificate Manager | `region`, `certificate_arn` |
| F5 BIG-IP | `partition`, `ssl_profile` |
| Cloudflare | `zone_id` |
| Dummy | `fail` |
| FortiGate | `vdom`, `import_scope`, `profile_suffix`, `default_ssl_profile` |
| Inventory agent | `host_ids`, `host_tags`, `cert_name`, `key_policy`, `require_all_success`, `wait_seconds` |
| Webhook | `timeout_seconds`, `metadata` |

FortiGate `replace_strategy`, `rebind_references` and `prune_old` decide what
the provider deletes, so a target cannot change them. The live list of every
provider field is `GET /api/deployer/v1/providers`.

## Permissions and roles

| Permission | Allows |
|---|---|
| `configurations:read` | list and read configurations (credentials redacted), list providers |
| `configurations:manage` | create, change, delete and test configurations |
| `targets:read` | list and read targets and their filters |
| `targets:manage` | create, change and delete targets and attachments |
| `jobs:read` | list and read jobs and their history; receive live job events |
| `jobs:manage` | cancel and retry jobs |
| `deploy:execute` | deploy, verify and roll back |
| `stats:read` | read the dashboard statistics |
| `backup:manage` | export and import the tenant's deployer setup |

| Module role | Permissions |
|---|---|
| Deployer administrator | all nine |
| Deployer operator | `configurations:read`, `targets:read`, `jobs:read`, `jobs:manage`, `deploy:execute` |
| Deployer viewer | `configurations:read`, `targets:read`, `jobs:read`, `stats:read` |

The platform's built-in roles also receive deployer permissions: `owner` and
`admin` all; `operator` all but `backup:manage`; `auditor` `stats:read` and
`jobs:read`; `member` `configurations:read`, `targets:read` and
`stats:read` (members do not see jobs).

## API

The browser API is under `/api/deployer/v1`, through the gateway. Changing
requests need the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

| Route | Permission |
|---|---|
| `GET /providers` | `configurations:read` |
| `GET /configurations`, `GET /configurations/{id}` | `configurations:read` |
| `POST /configurations`, `PUT /configurations/{id}`, `POST /configurations/{id}/remove`, `POST /configurations/validate` | `configurations:manage` |
| `GET /targets`, `GET /targets/{id}`, `GET /targets/{id}/configurations` | `targets:read` |
| `POST /targets`, `PUT /targets/{id}`, `POST /targets/{id}/remove`, `POST /targets/{id}/configurations`, `POST /targets/{id}/configurations/remove` | `targets:manage` |
| `POST /deploy` (one configuration), `POST /deploy/target`, `POST /deploy/configurations` | `deploy:execute` |
| `POST /deploy/{job_id}/verify`, `POST /deploy/{job_id}/rollback` | `deploy:execute` |
| `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `GET /jobs/{id}/children`, `GET /jobs/{id}/history`, `GET /jobs/{id}/result` | `jobs:read` |
| `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel`, `POST /jobs/{id}/retry` | `jobs:manage` |
| `GET /statistics`, `GET /statistics/tenant` | `stats:read` |
| `POST /backup/export`, `POST /backup/import` | `backup:manage` |

Deploy requests answer `202` with the job ID; the outcome arrives as live
events and on the job.

### Errors

| Status | `reason` | Typical cause |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_body` | invalid JSON or an unknown field |
| 403 | `forbidden` | the permission is missing |
| 404 | `not_found` | no such item in your tenant |
| 409 | `unsupported` | verify or rollback on a parent job or a provider without it |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | a field is invalid (`detail.fields` names it), the configuration is not active, or the target has no configurations |
| 422 | `credentials_rejected` | the endpoint refused the credentials during a test |

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| name of a configuration or target | 100 characters |
| filter pattern | 256 characters (longer never matches) |
| list page size | 200 |
| JSON request body | 64 KiB |
| automatic retries per job | 3 |
| job attempt timeout | `jobs.job_timeout_seconds` (default 300 s) |
| job retention | `jobs.cleanup_days` (default 30 days) |
